report:
Hello,

Sorry if this is a bit disjointed, I'm writing from a crowded supermarket and it's hard to concentrate. I'm emailing about my father's Lisinopril. He takes 2.5 mg once a day for his blood pressure and has been on it since 2019.

The latest bottle doesn't seem right. The number of tablets inside doesn't match what the packaging says should be there, and I think it's fewer. The label also looks off to me. I can't say exactly what's wrong with it, but it doesn't look like his earlier ones.

Because of the count, he ended up missing a dose. I'm not sure whether it was just one day or more than that, and I haven't been able to ask him again.

To be clear, nothing bad has happened to him that we know of. No new symptoms and no trouble. I just wanted this on record in case other people have had the same problem. I still have the bottle if you need details from it.

Please let me know what else you need from me.

Anthony Brooks
channel: email_reply: reply to the sender's email address (Anthony Brooks)
draft_message:
Dear Mr Brooks,

Thank you for getting in touch about your father's Lisinopril, and for the details you've given us. Please don't worry about the email being disjointed.

We would be grateful for a little more information:

1. How many days did your father go without his Lisinopril because of the tablet count? If you can, please ask him and let us know.
2. Since then, has he had any blood pressure readings (at home, at a pharmacy or at the doctor's) or any medical check-up? If so, what were the results?
3. Has he seen a doctor or nurse, or been given any treatment, because of the missed dose or for any other health reason since then?

Please keep the bottle and its packaging safe for now. We may ask you for details from it later.

You can answer by replying to this email. Thank you for your help.

Kind regards,
Drug Safety Team

report:
Hello,

Sorry for the delay in sending this over; the power just came back on here and I'm getting caught up. Passing along a report from a physician assistant in the US, who did not give a name when contacting us.

The PA described a male patient, age not provided, who was taking some blood pressure pill. The PA wasn't sure which one, and we don't have a product name, dose, or start date.

According to the PA, the patient appeared to have an allergic-type reaction to the pill. He also developed swelling, and he had stiffness in his joints and ongoing tiredness. The PA also reported that his liver and kidneys had stopped working properly, and that his existing condition got worse. The PA didn't say what that condition was. The patient was admitted to hospital.

No other medicines were mentioned. We don't know what the patient's outcome was or what was done with the blood pressure pill. I can try to go back to the PA for the missing details if that would help.

Regards,
Maria Ramirez, Drug Safety Associate, Kestrel Health Partners
channel: Partner case query: send to Maria Ramirez, Drug Safety Associate, Kestrel Health Partners, and ask her to go back to the US physician assistant. The PA gave no name or contact details, so there is no direct route to the PA.
draft_message:
Dear Maria,

Thank you for forwarding PSR-2022-81406, and for offering to go back to the physician assistant. Yes, please. We need two things to finish processing the case:

1. What is the name of the blood pressure medicine the patient was taking (brand or generic name)? If the PA can't recall it, please ask for any detail that could identify it. Examples are the active ingredient, drug class, manufacturer, tablet strength or appearance, or the dispensing pharmacy.

2. What was the outcome for the patient's reported events (for example recovered, still ongoing, worsened, or death)? Please include how long he was in hospital and whether he has been discharged.

Thank you for your help.

Kind regards,
Drug Safety

report:
Hello,

I'm writing quickly because I'm minding my neighbour's kids and they're running around behind me, so forgive the rushed email. I want to report something about a woman who has been taking Synthroid since 2021. Levothyroxine was also part of her medicine.

From what I understand, she developed an infection in her arteries, and her eyesight has got worse. She has also been told her bones are thinning. She had some kind of procedure and then had complications afterwards. She caught covid at some point too. Through all of this, the thyroid medicine didn't seem to be doing its job.

She ended up being admitted to hospital. I don't know the doses, the exact dates, or how she is doing now.

I'd rather not be contacted and I'm not leaving contact details. I just wanted this passed on to your safety team.

report:
Hello, I'm passing on a report from a pharmacist in France who phoned us today and did not give their name. A toddler was singing in the background for much of the call.

The pharmacist heard second-hand from a customer about someone that customer knows, who has taken Lipitor 20 mg once a day for high cholesterol since 2018. According to the story, the muscle tissue in this person's body became inflamed and started to die off. They were admitted to hospital, and the pharmacist understands they are now slowly recovering.

The pharmacist could not identify the person and had no other details. I have nothing further to add at the moment.

Camille Moreau, Drug Safety Associate, Halvern Therapeutics

draft_message:

Thank you for your report PSR-2022-77489 (Lipitor 20 mg, muscle inflammation and breakdown, France). We cannot process it yet because we have no identifiable patient. Could you ask the pharmacist, and through them the customer if possible, the following?

report:
Hello,

I'm writing this on my phone while sitting under the dryer at the hairdresser's, so apologies if it's a bit rambling. The woman doing my hair was chatting about someone she knows through a friend, and it stuck with me, so I thought I'd pass it on to you.

As I understand it, this person has been on Sertraline since around November 2019, for anxiety and low mood together. She said they had been feeling very nervous and jittery and got dizzy spells. They also seemed to have trouble keeping their attention on things and were feeling weak and drained a lot of the time. Apparently they'd also missed some doses of it at some point, though I don't know how often or why.

The nervousness and the dizziness have both cleared up now, I was told. I don't know whether the weakness or the concentration trouble have gone.

I can't tell you who the person is, and I don't know anything else about them, I'm afraid. I just wanted it noted.

Kind regards,
Claire Evans
channel: email_reply: reply to the sender's email address (Claire Evans)
draft_message:
Dear Ms Evans,

Thank you for taking the time to write to us about this. We appreciate it.

We have noted what you told us about the person taking sertraline. To record the report, we need a few details about the person themselves. Please share only what you know or can easily find out. We don't need their full name.

1. Do you know, or could you find out, the person's age (or approximate age) and whether they are male or female?
2. Do you know their initials, or any other detail that would help us tell this person apart from others, for example the country or region they live in?
3. If you can't find out any of this, would you be willing to ask your hairdresser to pass our contact details to the person, so they can contact us directly if they wish?

You can answer by replying to this email. Thank you for your help.

Kind regards,
Drug Safety Team

report:
I'm writing about my Synthroid. At my last refill, the tablets looked and felt different from what I normally get. They seemed crumbly and chalky, and a few broke apart when I took them out of the bottle. I think the pharmacy may have switched me to a different product without telling me, because the bottle looked unfamiliar too. I'm not sure who made them.

On a happier note, my daughter just passed her driving test, so it's been a busy week here. You can reply to this email or call me on 555-0163.
